segments.text: Fat from anywhere?
So a recent weight loss study that looked at where fat mass was lost found that areas of fat loss didn't change the risk factors for heart disease and stroke.
The important thing was losing fat.
While diet and exercise are unable to specifically target regions of fat deposits, fat mass loss from anywhere can improve the risk factors.
Online advertisements might tell you that a magic workout machine will reduce fat in one particular area
But we can't target fatty tissue the same way that we can target a specific muscle group
Total loss of fat through healthy diet and exercise is the best outcome for overall health
And reducing either the symptoms of chronic disease or the risk of developing diseases such as diabetes or heart disease
I see and what do you mean when you say a healthy diet?
Well if we look at just two key elements carbohydrates and fructose carbohydrates provide a quick energy supply that's easy for the body to use but the body and brain don't need carbohydrates.
Your body does need glucose which can be obtained from carbohydrates but glucose can also be obtained when it's converted from protein and fat.
This means the lower your carbohydrate intake, the more the body uses fat for energy
Fructose, which is found in fruit, is something you should definitely avoid if you want to help your body get rid of fat
It's true that fruit can be good for your health as it contains fibre and vitamins
But to lose fat from around your body, it is important to limit the intake of fruit
Fructose activates an enzyme which activates other enzymes causing the body to accumulate fat
What about those who do eat well but still can't lose fat from around their belly or anywhere else?
Well if you sleep for less than 6 hours a night that can certainly be a contributing factor
There was a study done over a 16 year period that took into account almost 70,000 women
and that study found that those who slept five hours or less a night
were 30% more likely to gain 13 or more kilograms
than those who slept seven hours.
Stress is another issue.
The stress hormone cortisol has been known to increase the amount of fat
a person's body maintains and to also enlarge your fat cells.
Higher levels of cortisol have been linked more specifically
to increase visceral fat.
Age is also an issue.
As you get older, your body changes how it loses and gains weight.
Both men and women experience a declining metabolic rate.
In addition to that, women have to deal with menopause,
and if a woman gains weight after menopause,
it's usually more likely to be in their bellies.
And what should people do if they're worried about the amount of fat
they have around their belly?
Well, remember that not all fat is the same.
and some overweight and obese people with a store of excess fat around the middle of the body
might also have more muscle mass which could be protective.
However, by the same token, if you have fat around the belly
and it's greater than the size of your hips,
you should see a doctor to assess your cardiovascular health and fat distribution.
